title: Sericulture waste‐derived biodiesel and biogas for sustainable dual‐fuel combustion: Energy efficiency and emission trade‐offs
content:
Abstract

This study evaluates silkworm pupae biodiesel (SWPB) as a renewable pilot fuel for biogas (BG) dual-fuel operation and investigates a full-load performance-emission compromise using surrogate-assisted optimization. Experiments were conducted on a single-cylinder direct-injection diesel engine at 1500 rpm over 0%–100% load using diesel, neat SWPB, and SWPB with BG supplied at 2, 4, and 6 liters per minute (LPM). At full load, SWPB-BG 6 LPM increased cylinder pressure, heat-release rate (HRR), and brake thermal efficiency (BTE) by 22.97%, 20.93%, and 15.79%, respectively, relative to diesel. Carbon monoxide (CO), hydrocarbon (HC), and nitrogen oxides (NOx) were higher by 18.57%, 12.28%, and 5.56%, respectively (the CO and HC differences are comparable to analyzer accuracy and are treated as indicative trends), whereas smoke opacity decreased by 30.23%. Within the experimentally investigated domain, quadratic response surfaces were used as local interpolation models. Equal-weight desirability analysis at 100% load indicated a performance–emission compromise in the low-BG-flow region, with a model-predicted value of 2.59 LPM (not distinguishable from the measured 2 LPM condition within instrument accuracy), corresponding to a BTE of 29.67%, CO of 0.0688%, HC of 55.36 ppm, NOx of 885 ppm, and smoke opacity of 40.23%. Because only three BG flow rates were experimentally tested and 2.59 LPM was not directly evaluated, this condition should be regarded as an interpolation-based candidate operating point requiring independent experimental validation.
